description: Compare the two AppendEntries entry paths for one out-of-window pure heartbeat: the normal RPC path (processRPC -> checkRPCHeader) must reject it, and the heartbeat fast path (processHeartbeat -> appendEntries) must apply the same guard so it cannot step the node down, advance its persisted term, adopt the sender as known leader or refresh its last contact.

harness.description: TestAssuranceHeartbeatFastPathProtocolGate builds three Raft nodes with all background goroutines disabled (conf.skipStartup), declares the out-of-window pure heartbeat, drives that request through processRPC on one node (recording rejection and whether any state changed) and through processHeartbeat on another (recording term/state/leader/last-contact before and after, and whether the guard was applied), and drives an in-window control request to show the difference is attributable to the header window rather than the request shape. CA_EVENT lines are emitted for the declaration, the normal-path result, the fast-path result and the control.
semantic_changes: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking processHeartbeat directly. That is the body of the handler installed by transport.SetHeartbeatHandler, and the package's own integration test demonstrates the callback contract by calling r.processHeartbeat(rpc) from inside a custom heartbeat handler; net_transport's fast path is reached only over TCP and network access is disabled in the execution sandbox, so the transport classification is declared as a sourced premise instead of being reproduced.
Nodes are constructed with conf.skipStartup = true, the pattern used by the package's own tests, so no background goroutines run and the request handlers can be driven without racing the main loop.
No protocol logic is modified: the harness only constructs requests and reads existing state accessors.

legality.derivation: S42 defines checkRPCHeader and the protocol-version window it enforces; S41 shows processRPC applying it before appendEntries; S40 shows processHeartbeat calling appendEntries with no such check; S16 shows the same function installed as the transport heartbeat callback; S43 shows net_transport classifying a pure AppendEntries as a heartbeat and calling that callback; S44 shows a library-authored handler invoking r.processHeartbeat(rpc) for the request, which is why the direct invocation used here is the production seam and not a shortcut around it; S45 shows the fast path is absent for InmemTransport, so the harness must reach the handler deliberately rather than through an in-process cluster; S46 documents skipStartup; S14 is the term persistence the fast path can trigger.
legality.applicability: Applies to a node whose transport implements the heartbeat fast path, receiving a pure AppendEntries heartbeat whose RPCHeader.ProtocolVersion is outside the window checkRPCHeader accepts. The harness fixes that window with the node default ProtocolVersionMax (3) and a request header version of 0, which S42 rejects because 0 < 3-1.
unresolved: Whether a peer outside the supported protocol window can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment is a premise about peers, not about this node; it is declared by the scenario and not exercised end to end.
The consequence on elections (whether repeated refreshes of last contact suffice to suppress this node's own election) is not measured here.
conflicts: processHeartbeat's own comment says it must only be called from the main thread while the transport invokes it from a connection goroutine; the harness follows the transport's real usage, and the fields it changes are individually lock- or atomic-protected.
alternatives: The fast path may intentionally assume an already-accepted peer, in which case the correct disposition is a documented assumption rather than a guard defect.

grounding.derivation: The obligation requires the same RPC-header compatibility decision on both entry paths. The event reports whether the fast path left term, state, leader identity and last contact untouched for a request the normal path independently rejects.
grounding.applicability: Evaluated only for a request declared out of window, and only when the normal path has independently rejected the same request shape on the same identity.

observable_properties.description: For an out-of-window pure heartbeat, the heartbeat fast path applies the same RPC-header guard as the normal path, leaving term, state, leader identity and last contact unchanged.

uncertainties: Reachability of an out-of-window peer that can produce a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment.
Whether the guard omission is deliberate design, making the correct disposition a documented assumption rather than a violation.
The election consequence of refreshing last contact on this path is not measured.
